explanations.explanation: That's right, baker. Elimelech's family leaves Bethlehem in Judah and goes to live in Moab when the famine hits. Ruth 1:1 says it plain.
Not Egypt. The family goes from Bethlehem in Judah to Moab because there is a famine in the land. Ruth 1:1 gives the place.
Not Edom. The text says they went to live in the land of Moab. Ruth 1:1 is clear about that.
Box-worthy! The other Moabite woman is Ruth. Ruth 1:4 names Orpah and Ruth side by side, just like that.
Not Rachel. Ruth 1:4 says the other woman is Ruth. That name is right there in the verse.
Not Dinah. The verse names the second woman Ruth, not Dinah. Ruth 1:4 says it straight.
That's a hard turn. Ruth 1:5 says both Mahlon and Chilion die, and Naomi is left without her sons and without her husband. The text keeps it plain and heavy.

explanations.answer: Her house in Moab burns down
explanations.explanation: No, the text does not say that. Ruth 1:5 says both of her sons die, and Naomi is left without her husband too. Nothing is said about a house burning.

explanations.answer: She falls sick and loses her sight
explanations.explanation: No, baker. Ruth 1:5 says Naomi is left without her sons and without her husband because both sons die. The verse does not say anything about sickness or sight.
Perfect bake! Naomi hears that the LORD has attended to His people by giving them food. Ruth 1:6 says the famine has turned and provision has come.
Not a king. Ruth 1:6 says the LORD had attended to His people by providing them with food. That is the provision named in the verse.
Not victory. Ruth 1:6 says the LORD gave His people food. The verse is about provision, not battle.

explanations.answer: Go back to their mothers' homes
explanations.explanation: Fine work, baker! Naomi tells her daughters-in-law to go back, each of them, to her mother's home. Ruth 1:8 says that right after she blesses them.

explanations.answer: Walk faster to beat the dark
explanations.explanation: No, that's not what Naomi says. Ruth 1:8 says she tells them to go back to their mother's home. The verse does not mention walking faster or beating the dark.

explanations.answer: Stay close to her the whole way
explanations.explanation: No. Naomi tells them to go back, each of them, to her mother's home. Ruth 1:8 is a send-home, not a stay-close order.
That's right. Naomi does speak about each of them finding rest in the home of a new husband. Ruth 1:9 says it as part of her send-off.
No, that part is in the text. Naomi says, May the LORD enable each of you to find rest in the home of your new husband. Ruth 1:9 says that right after she blesses them.

explanations.answer: We will return with you to your people
explanations.explanation: That's right, baker. Orpah and Ruth say they want to go back with Naomi to her people. Ruth 1:10 gives their answer after Naomi's blessing.

explanations.answer: We will stay in Moab and wait for you
explanations.explanation: No. Ruth 1:10 says they answer that they will return with Naomi to her people. The verse does not say they will stay behind in Moab.

explanations.answer: We will come visit you in Bethlehem
explanations.explanation: Not that. Ruth 1:10 says they will return with Naomi to her people. It is a return with her, not just a visit.

explanations.answer: Would you wait for them to grow up
explanations.explanation: That's the question Naomi asks. Ruth 1:13 says, would you wait for them to grow up? She is pressing the point that there is no practical husband for them from her womb.

explanations.answer: Would you raise them as your own
explanations.explanation: No, baker. Ruth 1:13 says Naomi asks whether they would wait for the sons to grow up. That is the question the verse gives.

explanations.answer: Would you go ahead to Bethlehem
explanations.explanation: No. Naomi's question in Ruth 1:13 is whether they would wait for them to grow up. Bethlehem is not the question there.

explanations.answer: The LORD's hand has turned against her
explanations.explanation: Baked just right! Naomi says it is more bitter for her because the hand of the LORD has gone out against her. Ruth 1:13 says that plainly.

explanations.answer: The people of Judah have turned against her
explanations.explanation: No, the verse does not say that. Naomi says the hand of the LORD has gone out against her. Ruth 1:13 gives that reason, not a rejection from Judah.

explanations.answer: The people of Moab have turned against her
explanations.explanation: No. Ruth 1:13 says Naomi's bitterness comes because the hand of the LORD has gone out against her. The verse does not say the people of Moab turned against her.
That's a keeper! Ruth 1:14 says Orpah kissed her mother-in-law goodbye. The verse is direct about it.
No, the verse says Orpah kissed her mother-in-law goodbye. Ruth 1:14 makes that clear before Ruth clings to Naomi.
Nope. Ruth 1:14 says Orpah goes back, but Ruth clings to Naomi. So Ruth does not go back home with Orpah.
Perfect bake! Ruth 1:14 says Orpah goes back, but Ruth clings to Naomi. Ruth does not turn around with her.
That's right. Naomi does tell Ruth to follow her sister-in-law back home, because Orpah has gone back to her people and her gods. Ruth 1:15 says it clearly.
No, baker. Ruth 1:15 says Naomi tells Ruth to follow her sister-in-law back home, after saying Orpah has gone back to her people and her gods. That is exactly what the verse says.

explanations.answer: Naomi's God will be her God
explanations.explanation: Perfect bake! Ruth says Naomi's people will be her people, and Naomi's God will be her God. Ruth 1:16 gives both parts of her promise.

explanations.answer: She will take care of Naomi's house
explanations.explanation: No, that is not what Ruth says. Ruth 1:16 says Naomi's people will be her people and Naomi's God will be her God. The verse does not mention Naomi's house.

explanations.answer: She will learn all the ways of Judah
explanations.explanation: No. Ruth 1:16 says Ruth promises Naomi's people and Naomi's God will be hers. It does not say she will learn all the ways of Judah.
That's right. Ruth says that nothing but death should separate her and Naomi. Ruth 1:17 says it with strong words.
No, the verse says death, not distance. Ruth 1:17 says may the LORD punish her if anything but death separates them. That is the word the text uses.
No. Ruth 1:17 says the only thing that should separate them is death. Marriage is not the word in the verse.

explanations.answer: She stops trying to persuade her
explanations.explanation: That's a keeper! Ruth has made her choice, and Naomi stops trying to persuade her. Ruth 1:18 says Naomi saw that Ruth was determined to go with her.

explanations.answer: She sends her back after Orpah
explanations.explanation: No. Ruth 1:18 says Naomi saw that Ruth was determined to go with her, so she stopped trying to persuade her. She does not send Ruth after Orpah.

explanations.answer: She tells her to wait in Moab
explanations.explanation: No, baker. Ruth 1:18 says Naomi stops trying to persuade Ruth. The verse does not say she tells Ruth to wait in Moab.
That's right. The women of the town exclaim, Can this be Naomi? Ruth 1:19 records their words when Naomi and Ruth arrive in Bethlehem.
No, that is not what the women say. Ruth 1:19 says they exclaim, Can this be Naomi? The verse gives that line, not this one.
No. Ruth 1:19 says the women of the town exclaim, Can this be Naomi? They recognize her and say her name.
Fine work, baker! Naomi tells the women to call her Mara. Ruth 1:20 says that name and explains why she wants it.
No. Ruth 1:20 says Naomi tells them to call her Mara. Hannah is not the name in the verse.
No, baker. Ruth 1:20 says Naomi wants to be called Mara. The text does not say Leah.
Nope. Naomi says, I went away full, but the LORD has brought me back empty. Ruth 1:21 says that, so the statement as written is not true.
That's right. Naomi says, I went away full, but the LORD has brought me back empty. Ruth 1:21 says the opposite of the statement.
Box-worthy! Ruth 1:22 says Naomi and Ruth arrive in Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest. That is the crop named in the verse.
No, baker. Ruth 1:22 says they arrive at the beginning of the barley harvest. Wheat is not the word used there.
No. Ruth 1:22 says the beginning of the barley harvest. Olive is not what the verse says.
